title: Quantum Algorithms and Hardness for Point-Count Approximation over Finite Fields
summary: We study the approximation of the number of solutions of Laurent polynomials over finite fields. For a Laurent polynomial \[f(x)=\sum_{j=1}^{s}a_jx^{u_j}\in \mathbb{F}_q[x_1^{\pm1},\ldots,x_n^{\pm1}], \] let $U$ be its augmented support matrix whose columns are $(1,u_j)$ with rank $ρ$ and $N(f) := \# \{x\in (\mathbb{F}_q^\times)^n \mid f(x)=0\}$ be its torus point count. Our first main result is a quantum algorithm that outputs $\widehat{N}(f)$ satisfying \[ |\widehat{N}(f) - N(f)| \le \varepsilon q^{n+s/2-ρ} \] with success probability $1-δ$.
